faq.a: An alloy is a mixture of a metal with one or more other elements, usually other metals or carbon, melted together. Alloys are designed to be stronger, harder, tougher or more rust-resistant than the pure metal.

In a pure metal all the atoms are the same size and pack in regular layers, so the layers can slide over each other fairly easily when you push. That is why pure gold, copper and aluminium bend easily.

faq.q: How are atoms arranged in a metal?
faq.a: Metal atoms pack closely in regular repeating patterns, held together by a sea of shared electrons. Real metals are made of many tiny crystals, or grains, each with its atoms in neat rows.
asks: What does a metal look like inside?

faq.a: Steel is iron and carbon; stainless steel adds chromium; bronze is copper and tin; brass is copper and zinc; solder is tin with other metals; and most jewellery gold is alloyed with silver or copper.

Stainless steel contains at least about 10.5 percent chromium. The chromium reacts with oxygen to form an invisible, very thin oxide layer that seals the surface and quickly re-forms if scratched, so the steel does not rust.

facts: 18 carat gold is 75 percent gold, alloyed with metals such as copper or silver.
Bronze, an alloy of copper and tin, gave its name to the Bronze Age, which began around 3300 BCE in the Near East.
